clinician.trajectory_summary: A 32-year-old man presented to the ED with severe right upper quadrant pain for 4 hours and jaundice noted over previous days. He had a history of milder meal-precipitated RUQ pain. Physical examination revealed icterus, positive Murphy sign, and RUQ tenderness. Laboratory studies showed elevated direct bilirubin (3.0 mg/dL), markedly elevated GGT (1153 IU/L) and ALT (685 IU/L), consistent with obstructive jaundice. Abdominal ultrasound identified cholelithiasis with a normal CBD diameter (6 mm), which was discordant with the degree of hyperbilirubinemia. MRCP revealed a well-defined broad-based pedunculated solid mass in the second portion of the duodenum inseparable from the ampulla of Vater, measuring 2.0×2.7×3.4 cm on staging CT, along with two small calculi in the lower CBD and multiple enlarged mesenteric lymph nodes. Endoscopy was performed with fine-needle aspiration biopsy of the mass; a stent was placed to relieve the obstruction. Histopathological examination of the biopsy specimens revealed a submucosal unencapsulated lesion composed of epithelioid, spindle, and ganglion-like cells with immunohistochemical positivity for S100, synaptophysin, and chromogranin, confirming the diagnosis of gangliocytic paraganglioma. During hospitalization, the patient developed fever and leukocytosis (13.0×10³/μL) consistent with cholangitis, which was treated with intravenous piperacillin/tazobactam with clinical and laboratory improvement. He was discharged on oral antibiotic therapy (ciprofloxacin and metronidazole).
